location: Minot Air Force Base, North Dakota
description: Born to a US Air Force father; the family moved repeatedly and lived in a trailer at one point while he was a child.

At age 12 he nearly lost an eye playing hide-and-seek when a stick penetrated it; a misdiagnosis and a later college re-injury left long-term vision problems that he cites in his healthcare messaging.
Graduated from MacArthur High School in Lawton after his family settled in Oklahoma.
Earned a BA in psychology in 1985 and served as student government president.
Earned an MBA in 1986.
Married Angela Allen in 1986; they had four children and five grandchildren before she filed for divorce in July 2025.

organization: University of Virginia School of Law
description: Earned a JD in 1991.
Practiced at a Dallas firm after law school.
Worked as in-house counsel for the retailer.
Opened his own practice focused on estate planning, probate and real estate law.

role_or_event: Won Republican primary runoff for House District 70
description: Beat Bill Vitz in a primary runoff with about 64 percent of the vote.
Won HD-70 with 28,012 votes in the general election.
Served five terms, winning re-election in 2004, 2006 and 2008 and running unopposed in 2010; authored anti-abortion legislation during this period.

role_or_event: Candidate for Speaker of the Texas House
description: Challenged incumbent Speaker Joe Straus and withdrew before the vote.
Placed first in the primary with about 44.4 percent and won the runoff with about 63.6 percent.
Defeated Democrat Sam Houston in the general election.
Served one term in the Senate before running for attorney general.
Finished first in the March primary with about 44.4 percent and beat Dan Branch in the May runoff with about 63.6 percent; won the general election without any Texas newspaper endorsement.

organization: Office of the Attorney General of Texas
description: Sworn in as attorney general; re-elected in 2018 and 2022. Created a human trafficking unit in 2015 and later quadrupled its funding.

role_or_event: Indicted by a Collin County grand jury
description: Indicted on two first-degree securities fraud counts and one third-degree count of failing to register as an investment adviser; the first indictment of a Texas attorney general in about three decades.

organization: Office of the Attorney General of Texas
description: Announced the raid on Backpage.com and the arrest of chief executive Carl Ferrer alongside California Attorney General Kamala Harris.

organization: Office of the Attorney General of Texas
description: Seven senior aides alleged bribery, abuse of office and improper favors to a developer donor; all had left the agency by the end of October 2020 and later settled for $3.3 million.

role_or_event: Lawsuit seeking to overturn the 2020 election
organization: Office of the Attorney General of Texas
description: Filed Texas v. Pennsylvania; the Supreme Court refused to hear the case, and the State Bar later brought a disciplinary action that was dropped in January 2025 on jurisdictional grounds.
The committee unanimously recommended impeachment on 20 articles after investigating the whistleblower allegations.

role_or_event: Suspended from the duties of attorney general
description: The Texas House impeached him 121-23 on 2023-05-27, suspending him from office; the Senate acquitted him on 2023-09-16, short of the 21 votes needed to convict.

role_or_event: Pretrial diversion agreement in the securities case
description: Entered a deferred prosecution agreement requiring community service and legal education; the charges were dismissed on 2025-06-18 with no admission of wrongdoing.
The Commission for Lawyer Discipline dropped the misconduct suit on jurisdictional grounds without any ruling on the merits.

role_or_event: Announced candidacy for the U.S. Senate
description: Announced a primary challenge to incumbent Senator John Cornyn on Fox News' The Ingraham Angle.
Angela Paxton, a state senator, filed for divorce citing biblical grounds and alleging at-fault serial adultery; the filing stated the couple had not lived together since June 2024.
No candidate won a majority in the March primary against Cornyn and Wesley Hunt, forcing a runoff.

Beat incumbent John Cornyn by more than 25 points with about 63.8 percent, despite being outspent roughly nine to one and holding Trump's endorsement; the first candidate in 56 years to defeat a sitting Texas senator in a primary.

organization: Office of the Attorney General of Texas
description: Halted property-tax increases in 132 municipalities under the 2025 property-tax growth law; a second tranche of more than 110 municipalities followed on 2026-08-17 after reviewing more than 1,000.

role_or_event: Lost the general election for U.S. Senate
description: Lost to James Talarico 42.97 percent to 55.06 percent in the most expensive Senate race in US history, with more than $560 million spent combined.
